name: Latitude
tagline: MCP-Native Agent Eval vs Open-Source Agent Observability Platform
oneLine: Open-source AI agent monitoring platform. Full observability into what's failing in production.
tldrVendor: Latitude is an open-source, MIT-licensed observability platform for production AI agents, operated by Latitude Data, S.L. in Barcelona. It ingests traces through a TypeScript or Python SDK or OpenTelemetry, groups failures into signals, scores sessions with LLM-as-judge, deterministic or JavaScript evaluations, tracks token cost, exposes an MCP server for coding agents, and can be self-hosted for free or run as Latitude Cloud.

vendorReasons.text: You need to self-host the entire platform for free on Docker Compose or Kubernetes, with your data staying in your own infrastructure.
You need recurring production failures auto-grouped into tracked signals with status, size and trend, Sentry-style.
You need a fix loop that dispatches Claude Code or Cursor with the failing traces and replays the fix against those traces.
You need a Cost dashboard with per-model economics and cache recommendations computed from your own traffic.
You need OpenTelemetry-native ingestion from any language, not only Python or TypeScript.

faq.question: What is the difference between Iris and Latitude?
faq.vendorPart: Latitude is an open-source, MIT-licensed platform for improving production AI agents: it captures agent traffic through a telemetry SDK or OpenTelemetry, groups repeated failures into signals, scores sessions with evaluations, and can be self-hosted or used as Latitude Cloud.

faq.question: Is Iris better than Latitude for MCP agent evaluation?
faq.vendorPart: Latitude offers things Iris does not: a free self-hostable platform with Sessions, Signals, Cost and Experiments views, LLM-as-judge and JavaScript evaluations that keep scoring live traffic, and a dispatch loop that hands failing traces to Claude Code or Cursor.
